meta.title: General Tech Services Website Redesign — Web Design Case Study | Teknoppy
meta.description: How Teknoppy redesigned generaltech.ae for a UAE ISO 17025 calibration lab — clearer accreditation trust signals, a separated service/product journey, and cross-linked equipment categories.

meta.label: Key Services
meta.value: Web Design, Website Structure & Information Architecture, SEO

paragraphs.text: General Tech Services is an EIAC & ENAS accredited ISO 17025 calibration laboratory and authorized distributor of 50+ industrial brands, operating out of Sharjah since 1998. With three distinct business lines — calibration, product supply, and engineering services — under one roof, the old site buried the lab's accreditation credibility and made it hard for visitors to tell whether they'd landed on a calibration provider or an equipment shop.

items.title: Accreditation buried, not led with
items.text: EIAC & ENAS ISO 17025 accreditation is General Tech's single strongest trust signal, but the old structure didn't put it in front of visitors early or consistently across the site.

items.title: Service and product journeys tangled together
items.text: Calibration services, engineering services, and the 50+ brand product catalogue competed for the same navigation space, making it unclear which path to take depending on what a visitor needed.

items.title: Categories and equipment left as dead ends
items.text: Product categories and calibration disciplines weren't cross-linked, so visitors researching one service (say, torque calibration) had no easy route to related equipment or adjacent disciplines.

paragraphs.text: Teknoppy's goal was to rebuild the site around a structure that puts accreditation trust front and center, cleanly separates the service and product journeys, and connects related categories and equipment so visitors — and search engines — can find their way through the full range of what General Tech Services offers.

sections.h2: A comprehensive range of services offered by Teknoppy and their outcomes

items.title: Accreditation-led structure
items.text: EIAC & ENAS ISO 17025 accreditation, the 15-discipline scope, and 28+ years of operating history are now surfaced in the hero, the "Why General Tech" section, and repeated as trust anchors through the page.

items.title: Three clear journeys: Calibration, Products, Services
items.text: Navigation and homepage sections now separate Calibration Capabilities, Product Supply, and Engineering Services into distinct, self-contained paths, each with its own entry point and CTA.

items.title: Cross-linked categories and disciplines
items.text: Calibration disciplines, product categories, and related services now link to each other, so a visitor on a torque calibration page can move naturally into torque tools or adjacent disciplines instead of hitting a dead end.

paragraphs.text: Discovery started with a full content and structure audit of the existing site against how visitors actually search for calibration and industrial supply services. From there, Teknoppy mapped a three-pillar architecture (Calibration / Products / Services) before touching design, then built the page templates in Astro to keep the accreditation and trust signals consistent across every service and product page.

sections.h2: General Tech Services' Final Outcome After Teknoppy's Work

items.q: What was the main goal of the redesign?
items.a: To put General Tech's ISO 17025 accreditation front and center and give visitors three clear paths — Calibration, Products, and Services — instead of one tangled navigation.

items.q: What platform was the new site built on?
items.a: The site was rebuilt on Astro for performance and to support the three-pillar content structure.

items.q: Did the redesign affect General Tech's existing rankings?
items.a: The restructure was scoped to avoid keyword cannibalization against General Tech's existing service and product pages — no overlapping targets were introduced.

items.q: Does the new site cover all of General Tech's calibration disciplines?
items.a: Yes — all 15 accredited calibration disciplines are represented with their own dedicated pages, cross-linked to related products and services.
